transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support. My name is Aaron. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Aaron. My full fibre broadband suddenly cut out about forty minutes ago while I was working, and the optical box on the wall has a flashing red light.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm really sorry to hear that, Liam. Losing your connection in the middle of a workday is very stressful. Let me get your account open and check the optical link right away.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks, I appreciate that. I work as a software architect from home and I have an urgent client deployment scheduled for this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we dig into the fiber connection, Liam, could you please confirm your full installation address and your four-digit account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure. It's 42 Meadowcroft Lane, Cheltenham, GL51 9NX, and the security PIN is 7419.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Liam. I've got your Gigafast 500 profile right here on my screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, hopefully you can see what went wrong from your end.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to make sure I understand the full picture: the broadband dropped out completely around forty minutes ago, the power light on your white wall unit is steady, but the LOS light is blinking red, and rebooting hasn't brought it back. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. It went off dead at about nine twenty. The PON light is completely off and the LOS light is blinking red.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, thank you. That white box mounted on the wall is your Optical Network Terminal, or ONT. When the LOS light blinks red, it means Loss of Signal from the street optical fiber.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I figured it was something with the incoming fiber itself rather than my computer setup.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you check where the thin white fiber cable plugs into the bottom of that ONT unit? Is it firmly seated or has it been knocked or bumped?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look. It's in the hallway cupboard under the stairs. The green connector looks clicked in tight. Nobody was near it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And following that thin white cable back towards the hole in the wall, do you see any sharp bends, pinching, or heavy objects pressing against the casing?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, it runs straight along the skirting board and into the outside wall box. No kinks or bends at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good. Now looking at the lights on your main S-Net Hub router, what color is the status light on the front bar?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's pulsing orange slowly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood. That confirms the router is functioning internally but isn't getting a WAN IP lease because of the optical drop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, does that mean the main fiber line in the street is broken?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm checking our network telemetry for the Cheltenham central headend right now. There are no reported trunk fiber breaks or major outages in GL51.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh that's good news at least. I was worried a utility digger had gone through a duct in the street.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Indeed. However, our port monitor shows your specific Optical Line Terminal port at the splitter cabinet has gone into a protective shutdown state.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A protective shutdown? Why would the cabinet do that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It usually happens if there was a momentary optical power fluctuation, a brief laser desynchronization, or an automated frame timeout.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you reset that remotely, or does an engineer have to drive out to the street cabinet?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can run an automated port reset and laser optical power re-calibration directly from my diagnostic console, Liam.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Brilliant, please let's try that right away.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I initiate the port bounce, could you check the black power adapter plugged into the ONT? Is it plugged directly into the wall socket or an extension lead?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's plugged directly into a single wall socket on the back wall of the cupboard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, direct wall power is always best for consistent optical voltage. Now I will start the remote exchange reset.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'm watching the box now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about a minute and a half to run the optical test cycle.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Liam. The line diagnostics have completed the remote port bounce.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You're welcome. I'm right here in front of the ONT cupboard now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take a look at the ONT lights right now. Has the red LOS light stopped flashing?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hold on... yes! The red light went completely dark, and now the PON light is flashing green rapidly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's exactly what we want to see. Flashing green on the PON light means it's establishing optical handshake and ranging with the exchange.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, it just went solid green now. Solid green on PON and solid green on Power.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's check the LAN light on the ONT. Is that light flickering green or amber?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the LAN light is flashing amber very quickly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That indicates data packets are flowing across the Ethernet link into your Hub router. What is the Hub front light doing now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The Hub light changed from pulsing orange to a solid white glow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Solid white means your router has successfully authenticated with the WAN gateway and obtained its public IP address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test my laptop. I'll open a browser window and see if I can get through to my company intranet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take your time, Liam. Let me know if web pages and services load cleanly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! My work dashboard just popped up immediately, and our internal code repository is loading normally. That's a huge relief.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you run a quick speed test on speedtest.net just to make sure your full bandwidth and low latency are restored?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running it right now... ping is seven milliseconds, download is five hundred and twelve megabits, upload is seventy-two megabits.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Five hundred and twelve megabits down and seventy-two up is right on target for your Gigafast 500 tier.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's fantastic. I was really stressed about missing my deployment meeting this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You mentioned earlier your ONT is in the under-stairs cupboard. Is there plenty of ventilation around the equipment in there?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, there is plenty of room around both units, nothing is stacked on top of them.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are all your other devices connecting properly as well, like mobile phones or tablets?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check my mobile. Yes, the Wi-Fi icon is back on with full bars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And is your television streaming box connected to the 5 gigahertz network or an Ethernet cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The television box is in the lounge on Wi-Fi, and it looks like the guide is working again too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. I've also applied a profile stability lock on your exchange port so it won't drop session during heavy traffic.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is brilliant proactive service. I really appreciate you doing that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have logged the diagnostic results and the optical power readings on your account ticket for reference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's very helpful in case anything ever happens again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Aaron, thank you so much for fixing that so quickly. You saved my afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my absolute pleasure helping you today, Liam. Is there anything else with your S-Net service that I can assist with?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything sorted out completely. Thanks again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Liam. Have a wonderful rest of your day and best of luck with your deployment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Aaron, take care. Goodbye.
